Key genes in tumorigenesis

Role of key genes in tumorigenesis. (A) This pathway is initiated by MAPK cascades and facilitated. ERK, JNK, and p38 constitute three distinct groups of MAPKs. ERK is activated by MEK1 and MEK2, JNK by MKK4 and MKK7, and p38 by MKK3 and MKK6. Once activated, MAPKs regulate the transcription of downstream transcription factors FOSB and JUN genes while enhancing the expression of AP-1 complex. When activated by AP-1 and other related cytokines, they are essential for controlling diverse physiological processes such as gene expression regulation, cell proliferation and death promotion, facilitation of cell differentiation and movement in response to cytokines or growth factors or harmful stimuli; additionally inducing oncogenic transformation. (B) Cancer cells primarily rely on glycolysis for energy production, facilitated by LDHC, which also leads to excessive lactate generation. This lactate is exported to TME through MCT, enabling cancer cells to maintain an acidic microenvironment that promotes immunosuppression and immune evasion. FH, fumarate hydratase; FOSB, FBJ murine osteosarcoma viral oncogene homolog B; IDH, isocitrate dehydrogenase; LDHC, lactate dehydrogenase C; MCT, monocarboxylate transporter 1; SDH, succinate dehydrogenase; TME, tumor microenvironment
